text:
$SHOP CEO: 今天，真正的 $NVDA 就此终结。

取而代之的，不过是一个披着英伟达外衣、徒有其形的仿冒品。

未来掌舵的，将不再是开创者，而只是一群守成的看管者。他们会竭力守护黄仁勋亲手点燃的那团火焰，却终究无法让它延续下去。
@aleabitoreddit 我也倾向于认为，英伟达从此走向衰落
@aleabitoreddit Is your AI thesis in any way shaken after this?

This is company specific. I’m still heavily bullish on AI given I see it as the most transformational technology in human history.

But there’s a lot of nuances like $NVDA under a different CEO not making the same aggressive architectural bets or financing as they did before.

Alongside implications on Korean/Taiwanese/Japanese supply chains around Nvidia’s ecosystem.

There’s going to be buybacks propping up share prices. $NVDA near term revenue and roadmaps are still in tact.

I think Nvidia going to $0 is overblown. A CFO leading Nvidia can preserve their economics.

But over the next 10 years without Jensen’s leadership, I don’t see Nvidia continuing to grow 70% Y/Y without making transformational bets.

That’s the nuance I’m trying to convey

Just to state the nuances of my opinion: Jensen is irreplaceable to $NVDA.

No other CEO can visit a chicken shop in Korea, noodle shop in Japan

And rally hundred of billions of capital and supply chain commitment into Nvidia’s next technological vision.

As for Nvidia: the their roadmap is intact, their existing commitment and revenues are still preserved under Jensen’s leadership.

They’ll still be around 5-10 years from now, given how fundamentally important they are to AI supply chains. 

Under a new leader they can still continue growing if AI demand is intact and maintain their current lines.

But I don’t know anyone who can possibly think that under anyone else, whether it’s Tim Cook or an accountant:

That Nvidia could compound 70% capacity constrained growth Y/Y, without a leader like Jensen making these transformational bets.

As for AI implications:

I’m heavily bullish directionally, given AI is the most transformational technology in human history.

- I expect some potential slowdown in Nvidia’s ecosystem.

I don’t think an accountant can make the same aggressive level of commitments to Neoclouds or supply chains in Taiwan, Korea, Japan beyond existing architectures.

Then rally the capital and trust to make it happen.

- I do expect the next CEO to be more politically aligned with Washington in restricting China GPU access

- I also see the next CEO being less supportive of open weight models (positive for OpenAI/Anthropic)

- I’m less optimistic on $NVDA maintaining their competitive advantages against $AMD, $AVGO, and hyperscalers.

One person doesn’t break the AI trade, I expect companies from optics to memory to still outperform.

However, my confidence in the next leg of Nvidia’s growth, beyond their current roadmap, has been shaken without Jensen Huang.

Playing with ATLAS from @theworldlabs

This is one of the most insanely cool AI tools I've seen yet. The creative possibilities this opens up are virtually endless. I've been using this for like 10 minutes and my jaw is on the floor.

One of the hardest parts of making Stalk was set consistency between shots. Image models, and especially GPT don't understand perspective and angles, and they're always pulling towards the average. If the average photo of a TV is from the front, a foreshortened side view is hard to get consistently. I tried text-only prompting, I tried using set references, I tried having Claude build me clay sets in Blender to use as framing references.

Now you can just... move the camera. These are from a single Midjourney image. I've only scratched the surface, I imagine this will be even more valuable for my friends making video games.
